answer.why: As an insider I'd tap it at once, because 'confirmed and substantive' is the exact phrase from the service: confirmation in the appointment, then substantive rather than acting. It tells me the designers know the real texture of the job, and I'd be curious whether they get the details right. 'Minister Salary' reads like a punchline or a Straits Times comment-section bait. It's funny, but I've heard that joke at every kopitiam since 2012. I'd probably tap it too out of curiosity, but the other title earns more trust.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, slightly cynical game about the salary benchmark controversy, probably with a clicker-style money chase and jokes about the million-dollar pay. I'd expect it to be shallow and made for outsiders. I'd brace for wrong details, like invented grades and a politics-heavy storyline that skips the actual work of the service.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider-flavoured career sim about the slow grind of promotions: acting appointments, confirmation, appraisal wording, postings, and the wait for a substantive title. I'd expect gentle humour about bureaucracy and a game that rewards patience. The risk is that outsiders won't understand the name at all, so the store page has to do a lot of work.

Rachel Goh, now age 37, Perm Sec (Staff Grade) at MOF, heading into politics. Game grades and ages are unrealistically fast (Perm Sec at 30). Stats: REP 44, STAND 80, INTEG 80, COMP 94.

best_moment.what: Publishing the raw feedback alongside the engagement report. It cost me STAND, but it felt like the one decision a real officer would agonise over, and it was the one time the game let me be a little brave.

worst_moment.what: The quiet years (Y6-8) were just tapping through with nothing to weigh; I could not tell what I was choosing between, and nothing registered.

skip_year.why: The background check. I disclosed everything, the folder was thin, and it felt like a step the game made me click through without any tension or consequence.

callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Legacy line: old minute papers still forwarded with my name taken off

answer.held_back_by: Low REP, mostly. I kept choosing competence and integrity over visibility, so the team had a weak candidate when it counted. The Y9 raw feedback probably cost me with the people who decide who gets invited. The game also never told me what REP really measured.
answer.ending_fair_why: The result was a narrow loss that I had been warned about (REP 44 against the 60 a single seat needed), and the card was kind. It did sting that Y9 and Y2, my two best calls, did not visibly pay off at the end.
answer.chase_next: The version where I stay in the service past Perm Sec, or take the single-seat route with REP above 60. I want to find out what the 'different life' actually pays and whether the Y2 recovery plan ever comes back.
answer.play_again_why: I want to see whether building REP early changes the election, and it is short enough to try on the MRT. I would be less keen if the quiet years stay empty.

tone_breaks.line: Perm Sec at 30 / retired as Permanent Secretary at age 37
tone_breaks.note: Pacing is unrealistic. Perm Secs are not appointed at 30, and nobody retires at 37 after one election loss. Also, 'Staff Grade' is not how a Perm Sec would be described.

tone_breaks.line: Rumour: no rung above Perm Sec; the next step is 'a different life'.
tone_breaks.note: Good line, and the tea invitation was a nice touch, but the political route is shown as the only exit, which is not how it works. Plenty of Perm Secs move to statutory boards or GLCs.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about whether your appraisals, grade and standing get confirmed, not about the salary. 'Minister Salary' makes it sound like the goal is money, but I only noticed the pay figure at the end.

RACHEL GOH · THE FINAL POSITION
Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough, and it was never going to be about you anyway.

RETIRED AS Permanent Secretary
AT AGE 37
LIFETIME EARNINGS $9.56M
INTEGRITY 80

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: It never needed to. That is what the scholarship was for.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: Remembered fondly in three divisions and one constituency. Your old minute papers are still forwarded, with your name taken off.
